real_estate.homebuilder: Tri-City inventory is up 25% from a year ago, and most of the growth is priced $1M to $1.5M.
real_estate.commentary:
Rates are where Friday left them. Mortgage News Daily has the 30-year at 7.43% and the 15-year at 7.10%, a step off Thursday's 52 week highs, and nothing reprices until Monday.

Today's three charts come from our own MLS exports, a year of them. Fremont, Newark and Union City have 412 homes for sale, counting active, new, back on market and coming soon. That is 25% more than the 329 on October 7, 2025, our earliest saved export, and about the same as the 408 a month ago.

The total held, but the mix moved. Fremont eased 9% in a month to 257, while Newark rose 21% to 88 and Union City 24% to 67. The three cities bottomed at 135 on January 2, peaked at 443 in late May, and sit 7% below that peak now.

Homes are also selling more slowly. 143 are pending across the three cities, against 158 a month ago and 152 a year ago, so there are 2.9 homes for sale for every one in contract, up from 2.2 a year ago. The new supply sits between $1M and $1.5M: 155 listings against 95 a year ago, up 63%, and now 38% of the inventory.

What this means for you: buyers between $1M and $1.5M have nearly as much choice as at the May peak, with more time to compare. At Fremont's median on market list price of $1,199,400 with 20% down, the $959,520 loan is high balance conforming here, and principal and interest is $6,663 a month at 7.43%, against $5,747 at the 5.99% 52 week low. Sellers in that band are competing with more listings than any other band, so price for it on day one.

• Board wide: 2,761 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 183 coming soon and 232 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 713 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 627 are on the market and 86 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 257 live, 198 active, 37 coming soon, 22 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,199,400 at $777 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 29 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 182, Milpitas 119, Newark 88, Union City 67.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,089,000 at $679 a square foot. 290 homes are priced under a million, and 164 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

stocks.note: Levels are Friday, September 25 at the closing bell. Markets are closed for the weekend.
stocks.news:
Stocks closed the week higher even with the 10-Year near 5.2%. The S&P 500 rose 1.21% on the week and the Nasdaq 2.06%, and the Dow's Friday rally ended a three week losing streak. Nothing trades again until Monday morning.

Sunday's newsletter is a history lesson on the 1970s, when cash lost ground to inflation year after year. The long view today is kinder to owners of assets: the S&P 500 has roughly doubled since the end of 2022, from 3,839.50 to Friday's 7,743.41. Past performance, as the fine print insists, guarantees nothing.

economy.note: The 10-Year, gold and silver are Friday, September 25: the Treasury daily yield curve close and the COMEX settlements against Thursday's. Brent is Friday's settlement of the ICE November contract, the front month until it expires Wednesday.
economy.commentary:
The 10-Year finished the week at 5.17%, a hair under Thursday's 5.18%, the highest close since 2007. Gold settled Friday at $4,321.20 and silver at $64.80. Brent gave back 2.14% to $104.32 on hopes that shipping through the Strait of Hormuz could reopen.

The Sunday newsletter compares today to 1979, when inflation ate cash savings. Its math checks out: a savings account paying 4.5%, taxed in the 22% bracket, keeps about 3.5%, and consumer prices rose 3.4% in the year to August, per the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Keeping up is not the same as getting ahead.

crypto.commentary: Crypto is the only market open on a Sunday, and it is barely moving. Bitcoin is at $84,462, up 0.20% over 24 hours, Ether is down 0.44% and XRP is down 0.76% at $1.51. Bitcoin has now spent five days near $84,000, since Wednesday's slide from about $86,600. Prices are live from CoinGecko at 3:08 PM PT.
